subject: Deployment mode & migration follow-up - Redwood options for Aurora Health
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Tom Lee <tom.lee@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@aurorahealth.com>
Date: 2027-05-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Deployment mode follow-up + ask list

Hi Tom / Priya -

Thanks again for the call this morning - really appreciate you walking us through Aurora's current stack and the mix of workloads you run. Below is a quick recap and a few follow-up questions so we can scope the right migration path (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC).

Recap (from our notes):
- Primary chat / customer-facing flows currently on OpenAI (API) for real-time assistance.
- A subset of fine-tuned models run on an internal GPU cluster for sensitive PHI workloads.
- Key priorities: latency at peak, predictable unit cost, and PHI-compliant data residency.

Follow-up questions (helps us recommend next steps):
1) Traffic profile: what are peak qps and typical request size (tokens) for chat?
2) SLOs: target p95 latency for user-facing chat and acceptable degradation window during rollout.
3) PHI split: which endpoints/data sets must remain in a private environment vs can use hosted?
4) Migration constraints: do you have a hard cutover date or are you expecting phased migration?
5) Procurement timeline & purchasing model: are you evaluating reserved capacity / committed spend this quarter?

What I'd propose: start with a short POC using Redwood Hosted API for non-PHI flows (fast time-to-value) while we evaluate Dedicated capacity or Private VPC for PHI. That lets you verify latency/cost on a representative workload and then move sensitive traffic to Dedicated or Private when procurement completes.

Attached: deployment-modes-one-pager.pdf (short summary), next-steps.xlsx (suggested POC scope & milestones).

If you can reply with answers to the 5 questions above, I'll loop in Dev (SE) to propose a technical deep-dive and draft an architecture for the POC.

Available times for a 45m technical session next week: Tue/Wed 10-12 PT, Thu 1-3 PT (also linked here: https://calendar.redwood.com/marissa/30min?slot=20270503T1600).

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Tom Lee <tom.lee@aurorahealth.com>

Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@aurorahealth.com>, procurement@aurorahealth.com
Date: 2027-05-01T12:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Deployment mode follow-up + ask list

Marissa -

Thanks for the summary and the clear next steps. Answers below inline.

1) Traffic profile: peak ~220 qps for the consumer chat endpoint, average request ~450 tokens. Background batch generation (reports) is much larger but can be scheduled.
2) SLOs: p95 target 250-300ms for chat responses. During rollout we can tolerate a 20% spike in latency for up to 2 hours, but anything beyond that needs a rollback plan.
3) PHI split: PHI must remain in our private environment (HIPAA). Non-PHI user messages can go to a hosted endpoint. We have strict logging/audit requirements for any PHI-related calls.
4) Migration constraints: phased. Priority is to move non-PHI traffic off OpenAI first, then evaluate options for PHI workloads. No hard cutover date - target to have procurement complete by end of Q3.
5) Procurement: procurement timeline is Q3; we are open to reserved capacity if cost math works. Procurement is on this thread (procurement@aurorahealth.com) for initial vendor conversations.

Attached is our security questionnaire that Priya completed earlier - security-questions.pdf.

Next steps: we'd like a technical session with Dev and an outline of the POC plan for non-PHI traffic. Thanks - Tom

Best,
Tom Lee
Director of AI Platforms, Aurora Health
Tom.Lee@aurorahealth.com

Tom / Priya / Procurement -

Great, thanks for the details - that helps a lot.

Proposed path based on your answers:
- Phase 1 (POC, non-PHI): Redwood Hosted API + request-level encryption for tokens in transit. Validate p95 latency and cost on a representative subset (we can replay a slice of production traffic).
- Phase 2 (Dedicated): If latency/cost objectives require it, move to Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) for predictable throughput and lower per-token cost. This also gives you isolation at the tenant level.
- Phase 3 (Private VPC / On-prem): For PHI-bound endpoints, we'd deploy Redwood Private in your VPC (or on-prem package) to meet HIPAA and audit requirements. Our Private offering supports KMS integration and audit log export.

For the POC we typically run a 4-week test: 1 week integration & replay, 2 weeks live validation, 1 week tuning and cost analysis. I attached a draft POC plan (proposed-poc-plan.docx) and a sample milestone sheet in next-steps.xlsx already sent.

Dev - I've looped you in to own the technical deep-dive. Can you confirm availability Tue/Wed 10-12 PT or Thu 1-3 PT and whether we should include any additional Redwood folks (SRE or product)?

Tom - would you be comfortable starting with a 1-2k rps equivalent replay subset so we can validate latency at scale? If so, please let us know the data handling constraints and any sample payloads we should use (sanitized or synthetic).

Thanks all - looking forward to the next session.

Best,
Marissa

Hi Tom / team -

Thanks - happy to run the technical deep-dive. A few quick notes from an SE perspective before the call so we can make the session productive:

- Replay size: a 1-2k rps equivalent subset is reasonable for an initial validation. For latency, we'll want a steady-state 10-15 minute window at peak to observe batching behavior and KV cache hit rates.
- Latency drivers: tokenization (client-side vs server-side), model choice/quantization, batching windows, and network egress. We can provide a small harness to run against your cluster or synthetic generator.
- Migration path considerations:
  * Hosted API: fastest to validate, zero infra on your side but not suitable for PHI unless shielded environment controls are applied.
  * Dedicated: gives predictable compute and lower unit cost; supports pinned model versions and reserved capacity. Good intermediate step.
  * Private VPC/on-prem: required for HIPAA/PHI; note that network egress and data ingress patterns can add cost and complexity - we'll want to size based on sustained throughput, not just peak bursts.
- Data/security: we'll need an EHR data handling doc for PHI endpoints and agreed redaction/sanitization rules for any production replay.
- Cost ballpark for initial Dedicated instance (approx): $Xk/month for a modest reserved pool (we'll firm up after we see token distribution).

Ask from Aurora before our call:
1) 1-2 representative sanitized payloads (or a schema) and a short sample of traffic (CSV with qps/tokens/peak windows).
2) Clarify which endpoints are strictly PHI so we can map network/design requirements.

I'll bring an SRE specialist if we see the need after the first technical session. Proposed times work for me; I'll accept whichever slot Tom picks on the calendar.

Cheers,
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.com
